conviction_note: Near-non-result: the bar is sourced and sits exactly where the guide floor is (Q3 9.3% margin = guided; FY consensus 10.4% vs guide 10.5-11%), so a narrowing to the low end is priced; two European peers (OPmobility guidance cut 2026-10-07 on volumes and Middle-East raw materials, Valeo Q3 OE -3.8% lfl on 2026-10-22) lean negative, while India PV demand +30.7%, a low FY bar, rising short interest after September downgrades and an upside-paid skew lean the other way; the findings net to about +0.1 and the scaled number is (2*0.48-1)*5.5 = -0.22, the gap being that the name's non-Q1 prints have been sold 5 of 5 times, which p_up carries and the findings do not.
bar: Autoliv's own consensus survey, updated 2026-10-19, 20 analysts (https://www.autoliv.com/investors/consensus-estimates): Q3 2026 sales $2,718M (range 2,638-2,765), adj. EBIT margin 9.3% (9.1-9.6), adj. EPS $2.18 (1.83-2.40); Q4 adj. EBIT 13.9%; FY2026 adj. EBIT 10.4% vs company guide 'around 10.5-11%' (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306698/alv-ex99_1.htm, which guided Q3 margin 'around the first-half level' = 9.3%). Benzinga's late-August $2.21 / $2.72B agrees. Q3 2025 base: sales $2,706M, adj. margin 10.0%, adj. EPS $2.32.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,931,143 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (~6.7% of 73.24M shares outstanding), 6.18 days to cover, up from 3,952,697 (5.4%) at 2026-07-31 - a 25% build after the Q2 print (https://equibles.com/stocks/alv/shortinterest, read 2026-10-22; 10-15 settlement not published until 2026-10-26). Benzinga cites 7.6% of float at 2026-09-11. Moderately elevated, not crowded. Baseline: event-implied move 5.48% (straddle 7.84% to 2026-11-20 net of ordinary vol; ATM spread 50% of mid, indicative only), 25d skew -2.83 vol points = upside paid, put/call OI 1.37 on only 1,719 contracts. Tape: +4.71% over 5 sessions, +3.13% over 20, 9.6% below the 52-week high. September sell-side turned cautious: TD Cowen downgrade to Hold (2026-09-08), Wolfe to Peer Perform (2026-09-23), Jefferies PT cut to $119 (2026-09-23) per aggregator snapshots.

findings.finding: The street already sits at the floor of the FY guide: Autoliv's own 2026-10-19 consensus (20 analysts) has FY2026 adj. EBIT margin at 10.4% against the company's 'around 10.5-11%' range, and Q4 at 13.9% (range 12.5-15.0%) where the guide midpoint needs roughly 15%; so a narrowing of the FY range to 'around 10.5%' at this print matches consensus, holding the full range would beat it, and only a cut below 10.5% is a new negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q2 (2026-07-17) the company kept the FY range but back-loaded it into Q4 and the stock fell 3.78% (baseline); at Q3 2025 it kept its FY margin guide and the stock fell 2.62%; the Q1 prints that rose (+6.82%, +5.56%) were the ones where the guide was first reassured.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced by construction: the consensus IS the market's bar. What is not priced is the asymmetry: if the market feared a cut below 10.5%, the 25d skew would be put-paid and short interest would have kept building into October; instead the skew is -2.83 (upside paid) and the stock rose 4.7% in five sessions.
findings.independence: The Q2 transcript (https://www.autoliv.com/sites/autoliv/files/pr/Autoliv_Q2_2026_webcast_transcript.pdf, 2026-07-17) shows the CEO declined to bias the range to either half and Wells Fargo computed ~15% Q4 needed for the midpoint, i.e. the street was told the Q4 step-up depends on raw-material compensation and engineering income. Shares the company document with the bar.

findings.finding: OPmobility (European exterior/module supplier) cut its 2026 operating-margin target from ~EUR500M to EUR430-450M on 2026-10-07, citing S&P Global Mobility's September production forecast cuts (especially China), European customers scaling back, and persistent raw-material/component inflation tied to the Middle East; its shares fell ~19.6% and dragged the sector - the same two drivers (volumes and Gulf-linked raw materials) Autoliv said its back-loaded Q4 and the $110M raw-material headwind depend on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autoliv's Q2 2026 print, where the raw-material headwind and the Q4 back-loading were first disclosed, cost 3.78% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer warnings are visible, so this is at most half unpriced: ALV has risen 4.7% in five sessions and 3.1% in twenty since, with upside skew, so the market is not treating OPmobility's raw-material read-across as a threat to Autoliv's Q4 compensation; if it were, ALV would have de-rated after 2026-10-08 and the skew would be put-paid.
findings.independence: Proxy: different products and a far larger European mix than Autoliv (EMEA 30% of ALV sales). Valeo's 2026-10-22 release (separate finding) says challenges 'have intensified over recent months'. The S&P downgrade on China is corroborated by CAAM's September production -8.7% (separate finding).

findings.finding: Valeo's Q3 2026 sales, published 2026-10-22: group -2.6% like-for-like, original equipment -3.8% lfl in an automotive market Valeo puts at -1.6%, FY targets confirmed, CEO saying challenges 'have intensified over recent months'; the stock fell about 4% on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autoliv's organic growth vs LVP has been the headline line; Q2 2026 +1.3pp outperformance with Americas -4.9pp and EMEA -1.0pp drew -3.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the release came out before the European open on 2026-10-22 and the sealed ALV close of 2026-10-22 already includes the day's sector reaction. What is left is the read that a -1.6% Q3 market (Valeo-weighted, Europe-heavy) is softer than the -2.5% FY LVP assumption implies for H2 composition.
findings.independence: OPmobility's 2026-10-07 warning points the same way (different document). Stellantis Q3 shipments -1% with Europe +10% (https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/news/6456975) points partly the other way for Europe.

findings.finding: China production deteriorated through Q3: CAAM output July -0.7%, August -4.7%, September -8.7% y/y (2.99M), Jan-Sep -4.5%, i.e. Q3 roughly -5% - in line with the -5% China LVP assumption under Autoliv's guide, but exiting the quarter worse, which bears on the Q4-loaded guide; Autoliv's China sales are 19% of group and 55% to Chinese OEMs that it outgrew by 40+pp in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China outperformance (+7.3pp in Q2 2026) has been the bullish line; the stock still fell 3.78% on that print because Americas underperformed.
findings.why_not_priced: Public CAAM data and inside the company's own China assumption, so largely priced; the residual is the September exit rate (-8.7%) feeding Q4 commentary. If priced as a threat, ALV would not have rallied into the print.
findings.independence: July and August from SMM / SteelOrbis (https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104073628-july-auto-production-and-sales-data-released-exports-exceed-1-million-units-for-two-consecutive-months-what-are-the-expectations-for-august-smm-special). OPmobility cites S&P's September China cut. Company-level offset: PV exports +64% y/y in September, which Autoliv says it serves from domestic plants (Q2 transcript).

findings.finding: India passenger-vehicle domestic sales rose 30.7% y/y to 1,360,687 units in July-September 2026 (SIAM), against Autoliv's Q2 India organic growth of 36% and ~20pp outperformance; India is the main engine of the Asia-ex-China region (19% of sales) and supports Q3 organic growth above LVP.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Asia-ex-China outperformance (+5.9pp) was reported in Q2 2026 and did not prevent a -3.78% day; the line has not been what the stock trades on.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (SIAM Q2 FY2026-27 release; URL not dated, SIAM figures are for Jul-Sep 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the company already guided 'continued significant outperformance' in India. A bigger-than-modelled India quarter would show up in consensus sales above $2,718M; the survey's high is only $2,765M (+1.7%), so the street is not carrying a large India surprise. Net of the rest: India is a single-digit share of group sales, so even +30% volume adds well under 1% to group organic growth, and Americas (32%) underperformed by 4.9pp last quarter.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript (company) documents 36% India organic growth and 20% annual content growth; different source from SIAM.

findings.finding: The euro weakened through Q3 2026 (Banque de France end-September EUR/USD 1.1355, from 1.1596 end-August; 2026 low 1.1325 in June) against roughly 1.17 a year earlier, so the euro leg of the FX translation tailwind Autoliv guided at '+2.5% on net sales' for the year is turning negative in Q3; the net effect depends on CNY and other currencies not checked here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was a +$62M sales tailwind in Q2 2026 and the CFO said margin expansion is 'supported by FX'; no history of a stock reaction to FX alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts update FX mechanically, so the sales bar ($2,718M, +0.4% y/y) likely already holds it; the residual is whether the FY 'FX +2.5%' line in guidance is lowered, which would look like a reported sales-guide cut to anyone reading the headline.
findings.independence: none (macro series; transmission not confirmed by the company).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print leans short and cautious, not long: short interest rose 25% from 3.95M (2026-07-31) to 4.93M shares (2026-09-30, ~6.7% of shares, 6.2 days to cover), and Wolfe (2026-09-23, flat 2027 sales, profits could fall below expectations) and TD Cowen (2026-09-08) downgraded to neutral in September, while the option market pays for upside (skew -2.83) and the stock has bounced 4.7% in five sessions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed squeeze history on this name; 6 days to cover is moderate.
findings.why_not_priced: Short-interest builds and downgrades are public; what they do is lower the bar for a relief move on an in-line Q3 with the FY range intact. If the market were positioned long into the print, the skew would not be call-paid on a name with 5 of 7 negative print reactions.
findings.independence: Wolfe downgrade dated 2026-09-23 at https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/autoliv-aktie-wolfe-research-senkt-rating-auf-peer-perform-2027-bleibt-schwierig; skew from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Autoliv's large OEM customers that have reported Q3 look steady: GM's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20) printed $50.0B revenue and $4.1B EBIT-adjusted and narrowed FY guidance with a new $20B buyback; Stellantis' Q3 consolidated shipments were ~1.30M, -1% y/y, with Enlarged Europe +10% - no sign of a Q3 volume collapse in the Americas or Europe (Autoliv's 32% and 30% regions).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Americas underperformance (-4.9pp vs LVP) was the weak spot of Q2 2026, -3.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and largely priced; it argues against a sales miss rather than for a beat, consistent with the stock's 5-day rise.
findings.independence: Stellantis Q3 shipments https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/news/6456975 (different company, different document).

outside_window.finding: FINRA short interest for the 2026-10-15 settlement is published 2026-10-26, after the exit; the model estimate on equibles is ~4.98M shares, i.e. no further build.
Forvia's Q3 2026 sales (production read for Europe/China) are due 2026-11-02.

baseline_tension: Roughly neutral against the baseline: the negative peer reads (OPmobility, Valeo) cut against the upside-paid skew and the 4.7% five-day run-up, while the low FY bar and the short build agree with them; the reaction history (5 of 7 prints down, every non-Q1 print down) is the strongest directional fact and keeps p_up just under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide / verify bar): consensus FY 10.4% sits at the guide floor, so a narrowing to ~10.5% is priced; guidance-bar finding cut +1.0 -> +0.6; China -5% is inside the company's own LVP assumption, -0.5 -> -0.3.
Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): OPmobility is a different-product peer with heavier European mix; -1.5 -> -1.0.
Rule 7 / timing: Valeo's release came before the sealed 2026-10-22 close, so its reaction is in the entry price; -0.8 -> -0.3.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): India is a single-digit share of group sales and Americas underperformed last quarter; +0.7 -> +0.5.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked, 6.7% of shares / 6.2 days is moderate not crowded; positioning finding trimmed +0.8 -> +0.6.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not reaction): non-Q1 prints sold 5 of 5 times; p_up 47 -> 48 only because the low FY bar offsets it, abs_move left at 5.5.
